scoring.summary: Every requirement is worth 1 point. The score is the number of the 24 requirements assessed as MET.

rules.summary: A requirement is MET only when every applicable assessment objective is satisfied.
rules.quote: Not Met. One or more applicable objectives for the security requirement is not satisfied.

rules.summary: An objective assessed N/A counts as MET.
rules.quote: an assessment objective assessed as N/A is equivalent to the same assessment objective being assessed as MET

rules.summary: Each Level 3 requirement is worth 1 point; the score is the number MET (maximum 24).
rules.quote: All CMMC Level 3 security requirements use a value of one (1) point for each security requirement.

rules.summary: Final Level 2 (C3PAO) status for the same assessment scope is required before a Level 3 assessment can start.
rules.quote: A CMMC Status of Final Level 2 (C3PAO) for information systems within the Level 3 CMMC Assessment Scope is a prerequisite to undergo a Level 3 certification assessment.

rules.summary: The Level 2 assessment must have the maximum score (every Level 2 requirement MET) before Level 3 can be initiated.
rules.quote: A maximum score on the Level 2 certification assessment is required to be eligible to initiate a Level 3 certification assessment.

rules.summary: Where an assessment objective uses an organization-defined or periodic interval, the interval may be no longer than one year.
rules.quote: As used in many requirements within CMMC, the interval length is organization-defined to provided contractor flexibility, with an interval length of no more than one year.

rules.summary: Conditional status needs at least 80% of the requirements MET (20 of 24), with no excluded requirement on the POA&M.
rules.quote: The assessment score divided by the total number of CMMC Level 3 security requirements is greater than or equal to 0.8

rules.summary: Seven requirements can never go on a POA&M and must be MET at assessment; any other NOT MET requirement may be deferred.
rules.quote: The POA&M does not include any of following security requirements:

rules.summary: Every POA&M item must be closed and confirmed by a DCMA DIBCAC closeout assessment within 180 days, or Conditional status expires.
rules.quote: The closing of a POA&M must be confirmed by a POA&M closeout assessment within 180-days of the Conditional CMMC Status Date

rules.summary: Final status requires all 24 requirements to be MET, at assessment or after POA&M closeout.
rules.quote: The OSC must complete and achieve a MET result for all security requirements specified in table 1 to § 170.14(c)(4) to achieve the CMMC Status of Level 3 (DIBCAC).

rules.summary: The Level 3 assessment must be repeated every three years.
rules.quote: the Level 3 certification assessment must be performed every three years for all information systems within the Level 3 CMMC Assessment Scope

rules.summary: A Level 2 (C3PAO) assessment must also be repeated every three years to keep Level 3 status.
rules.quote: a Level 2 (C3PAO) certification assessment must also be conducted every three years to maintain CMMC Level 3 (DIBCAC) status

rules.summary: The Affirming Official must affirm Level 3 after each assessment and POA&M closeout and every year, and must also affirm Level 2 (C3PAO) every year.
rules.quote: OSCs must annually affirm their CMMC Status of Level 2 (C3PAO) in addition to their CMMC Status of Level 3 (DIBCAC) to maintain eligibility for contracts requiring compliance with Level 3.

consequences.summary: Contracts that require CMMC Level 3 cannot be awarded until Conditional or Final Level 3 status is achieved and affirmed in SPRS.
consequences.quote: Prior to award of any contract or subcontract with requirement for CMMC Status of Level 3 (DIBCAC), the following two requirements must be met

consequences.summary: If Conditional status expires during a contract, standard contractual remedies apply and the company cannot win further awards that need Level 3.
consequences.quote: the OSC will be ineligible for additional awards with a requirement for the CMMC Status of Level 3 (DIBCAC) for the information system within the CMMC Assessment Scope until such time as a new CMMC Status is achieved

glossary.definition: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification, the Department of Defense program that verifies contractors protect federal contract and controlled information.
Controlled Unclassified Information: government information that is not classified but must still be protected.
Defense Industrial Base Cybersecurity Assessment Center, the DCMA team that performs Level 3 assessments.
CMMC Third-Party Assessment Organization, an authorized body that performs Level 2 certification assessments.
Organization-defined parameter: a value in a requirement, such as a frequency; for Level 3 the DoD has set these values.
Plan of Action and Milestones: the documented plan for closing requirements that are not yet met.
System Security Plan: the document that describes the system in scope and how each requirement is implemented.
Supplier Performance Risk System, where contractors record assessment results and affirmations.
Advanced persistent threat: a well-resourced adversary that pursues long-term access to a target.
